genesis.18.p1.b1.text: Then the LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent.

genesis.18.p1.b2.text: And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby.

genesis.18.p1.b3.text: When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.

genesis.18.p2.b4.text: My lord … if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass your servant by.

genesis.18.p2.b5.text: Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.

genesis.18.p2.b6.text: And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves. … After that, you may continue on your way.

genesis.18.p2.b7.text: Yes … you may do as you have said.

genesis.18.p3.b8.text: Quick! Prepare three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread.

genesis.18.p3.b9.text: Meanwhile, Abraham ran to the herd, selected a tender and choice calf, and gave it to a servant …

genesis.18.p3.b10.text: Then Abraham brought curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and he set them before the men and stood by them under the tree as they ate.

genesis.18.p4.b13.text: I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son!

genesis.18.p4.b14.text: And Abraham and Sarah were already old and well along in years …

genesis.18.p4.b15.text: After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?

genesis.18.p5.b16.text: Why did Sarah laugh and say, ‘Can I really bear a child when I am old?’

genesis.18.p5.b17.text: Is anything too difficult for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you—in about a year—and Sarah will have a son.

genesis.18.p6.b20.text: When the men got up to leave, they looked out over Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them off.

genesis.18.p6.b21.text: Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?

genesis.18.p6.b22.text: The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Because their sin is so grievous …

genesis.18.p6.b23.text: I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me …

genesis.18.p7.b24.text: And the two men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.

genesis.18.p7.b25.text: Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?

genesis.18.p7.b26.text: Far be it from You to do such a thing—to kill the righteous with the wicked … Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?

genesis.18.p7.b27.text: If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place.

genesis.18.p8.b28.text: Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord—though I am but dust and ashes—

genesis.18.p8.b29.text: If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it.

genesis.18.p8.b31.text: May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak further. Suppose thirty are found there?

genesis.18.p9.b32.text: Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?

genesis.18.p9.b33.text: May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?

genesis.18.p9.b34.text: On account of the ten, I will not destroy it.

genesis.18.p9.b35.text: When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home.
